parts: A humanoid robot just sank seven bean bags in a row.
Its teacher? One video of a person playing.
Google just released Gemini 4 Argon, its newest frontier AI model.
In an internal test, Argon watched a person play cornhole,
mapped the scene, and wrote its own physics simulation to practise in.
Then the skill moved onto a real humanoid, Apptronik's Apollo.
After a few warm-up throws: seven straight shots.
Google says that turns weeks of simulation work into hours.
The catch: it's Google's own demo of one simple game, not an independent test.
For builders: the next robot skill may start as a video, not as code.
